review_note: Injective sheaves of O-modules remain injective among O-module presheaves on a ringed site. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For the ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ is the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules, and $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$ is the category of modules over the underlying presheaf of rings; forgetting the sheaf condition embeds the former in the latter.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
An injective sheaf of modules is also injective as an
object in the category $\textit{PMod}(\mathcal{O})$.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.
conclusions: $\mathcal I$, as a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules, is injective in $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-module-injective-presheaf}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
An injective sheaf of modules is also injective as an
object in the category $\textit{PMod}(\mathcal{O})$.

review_note: Right-derived inclusion from module sheaves to module presheaves recovers U↦H^p(U,F). Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
hold_reason: The source writes Mod(C), PMod(C) rather than Mod(O), PMod(O), leaving module-category notation ambiguous in the ready statement.

review_note: An injective O-module sheaf has H⁰ Čech equal to its sections and H^p Čech zero in positive degrees. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For a covering $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)$ is Čech cohomology of the $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $\mathcal I$ regarded as a presheaf of abelian groups; here injectivity is in the category $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, not a separate assumption of injectivity as an abelian sheaf.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective $\mathcal{O}$-module, i.e., an injective
object of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$. Then
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathcal{I}(U) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.
$\mathcal U$ is a covering of an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$.
$\mathcal I$ is an injective object of $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$.
conclusions: $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)\cong\mathcal I(U)$ and $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I)=0$ for every $p>0$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be an injective $\mathcal{O}$-module, i.e., an injective
object of $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$. Then
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{I}) =
\left\{
\begin{matrix}
\mathcal{I}(U) & \text{if} & p = 0 \\
0 & \text{if} & p > 0
\end{matrix}
\right.
$$

review_note: Cohomology of O-module F equals underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology globally and over any site object U. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
Let $\mathcal F_{ab}$ denote the abelian sheaf underlying an $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal F$. The two cohomology functors in the comparisons are the derived section functors on $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and on $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)$, respectively; the underlying abelian groups are compared, even when module cohomology has additional scalar structure.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-module, and denote
$\mathcal{F}_{ab}$ the underlying sheaf of abelian groups.
Then we have
$$
H^i(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_{ab})
=
H^i(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})
$$
and for any object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we also have
$$
H^i(U, \mathcal{F}_{ab})
=
H^i(U, \mathcal{F}).
$$
Here the left hand side is cohomology computed in
$\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$ and the right hand side
is cohomology computed in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site with a sheaf of rings $\mathcal O$.
$\mathcal F$ is an $\mathcal O$-module and $\mathcal F_{ab}$ its underlying abelian sheaf.
conclusions: For every $i\ge0$, $H^i_{\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)}(\mathcal C,\mathcal F_{ab})\cong H^i_{\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal C,\mathcal F)$ as abelian groups.
For every $U\in\mathcal C$ and every $i\ge0$, $H^i_{\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C)}(U,\mathcal F_{ab})\cong H^i_{\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)}(U,\mathcal F)$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\mathcal{O}$-module, and denote
$\mathcal{F}_{ab}$ the underlying sheaf of abelian groups.
Then we have
$$
H^i(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}_{ab})
=
H^i(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F})
$$
and for any object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we also have
$$
H^i(U, \mathcal{F}_{ab})
=
H^i(U, \mathcal{F}).
$$
Here the left hand side is cohomology computed in
$\textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$ and the right hand side
is cohomology computed in $\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O})$.

review_note: Cohomology of a product of abelian sheaves maps isomorphically to product in degree zero and injectively in degree one. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
In the category of abelian sheaves on a site, $\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i$ denotes the sheaf product. For an object $U$, the projections induce a canonical comparison from the cohomology of this product to the product of the individual cohomology groups.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $I$ be a set. For $i \in I$ let 
$\mathcal{F}_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$. Let
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. The canonical map
$$
H^p(U, \prod\nolimits_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \in I} H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for $p = 0$ and injective for $p = 1$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site, $I$ a set, and $(\mathcal F_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: $H^0(U,\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i)\to\prod_i H^0(U,\mathcal F_i)$ is an isomorphism.
$H^1(U,\prod_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i)\to\prod_i H^1(U,\mathcal F_i)$ is injective (not asserted surjective).
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-products}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $I$ be a set. For $i \in I$ let 
$\mathcal{F}_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$. Let
$U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. The canonical map
$$
H^p(U, \prod\nolimits_{i \in I} \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
\prod\nolimits_{i \in I} H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for $p = 0$ and injective for $p = 1$.

review_note: A monomorphism of site objects induces surjectivity on sections of any injective O-module sheaf. Checked prepared statement against its pinned original-source theorem excerpt in Stage A; source proofs/remarks not opened. Non-authoritative preliminary verdict.
statement:
For any morphism of site objects $a:U'\to U$, the map $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal I(U')$ is the ordinary presheaf restriction along $a$. The condition that $a$ is a monomorphism is a categorical condition in $\mathcal C$; no topological open-immersion condition is added.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $a : U' \to U$ be a
monomorphism in $\mathcal{C}$. Then for any injective $\mathcal{O}$-module
$\mathcal{I}$ the restriction mapping $\mathcal{I}(U) \to \mathcal{I}(U')$
is surjective.
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.
$a:U'\to U$ is a monomorphism in $\mathcal C$.
$\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O$-module sheaf.
conclusions: The restriction homomorphism $\mathcal I(U)\to\mathcal I(U')$ is surjective.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $a : U' \to U$ be a
monomorphism in $\mathcal{C}$. Then for any injective $\mathcal{O}$-module
$\mathcal{I}$ the restriction mapping $\mathcal{I}(U) \to \mathcal{I}(U')$
is surjective.
